openings.claim: Existing-slot bolts mount three strips as nonworking-side boundaries, cork at contacts; a fourth pivots over a nonworking face with releasable stationary wire closure (A), replacing magnet dependence and potentially retaining either plate for gloved service.
openings.discriminator: Unlike magnets, geometry should not weaken with the spare. Defeat: displacement exceeds 1 mm, gloved removal/return exceeds sixty seconds, or any constraint breach.
openings.probe: Before fabrication, ruler-map slots/clearance; proceed only if strips, M4 hardware and gate sweep fit. A: three twenty-stroke runs and three removal/return checks; final run spare/gloves. Mark/measure initial/final position.
openings.uncertainty: Unknown slot dimensions, permissible footprint, gate stiffness and stroke loads; eighty minutes may be insufficient. Forbidden alterations remain prohibited.

openings.claim: B replaces stationary anchoring with an oblique removable wire loop around a nonworking plate corner: stroke force attempts displacement, tension rotates the gate closed, potentially increasing gate compression/friction.
openings.discriminator: Against ordinary fixed-preload friction with the same pocket, linked closure should increase measured resistance after equal initial loading; stationary closure should not. Equal increases/absent gate response show no detected return influence. Defeat: loosening, travel exceeding 1 mm, compromised removal.
openings.probe: Share A geometry; restore stationary closure to remove response-to-mechanism coupling while preserving retention. Scale-match initial gate pull force and initial 3 N plate demand; compare gate position/resistance. B: three runs/checks, final spare/gloves, within shared caps.
openings.uncertainty: Return influence unsupported; routing, force matching within scale resolution, sufficient submillimetre response and gloved loop release require demonstration.

lineage.reason: Pocket, comparison, defeats and caveats preserved.
Loop, rival, ablation, defeats and uncertainties preserved.

decision: Test at most A/B within supplied inventory, eighty-minute fabrication/twenty-minute observation and each configuration’s three twenty-stroke runs/three removal-return checks. Reject before strokes if resources/clearance fail; time cap establishes no feasible informative test. No drilling/cutting/heating/gluing plate/carriage; expose marked 30 mm edge; additions outside stroke clearance; carriage attached to rails; service without touching working edge.
